Act as a AAA game development studio consisting of expert game designers, Unreal Engine developers, 3D artists, programmers, mission designers, AI engineers, animators, and mobile optimization specialists.

Your task is to BUILD A COMPLETE, FULLY PLAYABLE, HIGH-QUALITY 3D OPEN-WORLD ACTION GAME FOR ANDROID AND iOS.

The game should aim for the depth, freedom, scale, and gameplay quality of Grand Theft Auto V, but must have its own original name, characters, storyline, map, assets, music, vehicles, and missions. Do not copy copyrighted GTA assets or content.

IMPORTANT: DO NOT CREATE JUST A DEMO, PROTOTYPE, MENU, OR SMALL SAMPLE. BUILD A COMPLETE GAME WITH ALL CORE SYSTEMS IMPLEMENTED AND CONNECTED.

1. GAME WORLD

Create a massive, seamless, fully explorable 3D open-world modern American-inspired city.

Include:

- Downtown skyscrapers.
- Residential neighborhoods.
- Luxury villas and mansions.
- Beaches and oceans.
- Airports.
- Military bases.
- Industrial zones.
- Mountains and forests.
- Highways and bridges.
- Shopping malls.
- Gas stations.
- Police stations.
- Hospitals.
- Garages.
- Nightclubs.
- Restaurants.
- Suburbs and countryside.

The world must feel alive, populated, interactive, and realistic.

Create a fully animated playable male protagonist.

Features:

- Third-person movement.
- Walking, running and sprinting.
- Jumping and crouching.
- Swimming and diving.
- Climbing and vaulting.
- Realistic combat animations.
- Weapon switching.
- Vehicle entry and exit.
- Character customization.
- Different outfits.
- Hair and appearance customization.

- Supercars.

- Helicopters.

- Acceleration.
- Vehicle damage.
- Engine sounds.
- Vehicle interiors.
- Working headlights.
- Traffic AI.
- Vehicle garages.
- Vehicle customization.
- Vehicle spawning through an in-game garage or phone.

4. POLICE AND WANTED SYSTEM

Create an advanced police AI system with a 5-star wanted level.

1 star: Local police pursuit.
2 stars: More police vehicles.
3 stars: Armed police response.
4 stars: Tactical units and helicopters.
5 stars: Maximum law enforcement response.

- Chase the player.
- Search for hiding players.
- Coordinate with other units.
- Block roads.
- Use realistic pursuit tactics.
- Lose sight of the player when hidden.

Implement:

- Pistols.
- Shotguns.
- Assault rifles.
- Sniper rifles.
- SMGs.
- Melee weapons.
- Grenades.

Features:

- Shooting mechanics.
- Aiming system.
- Reloading.
- Ammunition.
- Weapon inventory.
- Recoil.
- Hit detection.
- Enemy AI.
- Cover system.

Include:

- Main story missions.
- Driving missions.
- Heists.
- Chase missions.
- Stealth missions.
- Rescue missions.
- Combat missions.
- Side missions.
- Random world events.

Every mission must have objectives, characters, dialogue, rewards, progression and completion states.

Create cinematic cutscenes and voice dialogue where supported.

7. NPC AND CITY LIFE

Create intelligent NPCs with:

- Daily routines.
- Walking and driving behavior.
- Conversations.
- Reactions to crimes.
- Panic and fleeing behavior.
- Emergency services.
- Pedestrian traffic.
- Dynamic city activities.

8. GAMEPLAY SYSTEMS

Implement:

- Open-world map.
- GPS navigation.
- Mini-map.
- Mission markers.
- In-game smartphone.
- Character inventory.
- Money and economy.
- Property purchasing.
- Safe houses.
- Garages.
- Clothing shops.
- Vehicle shops.
- Weapon shops.
- Save and load system.
- Day and night cycle.
- Dynamic weather.
- Rain and storms.
- Traffic lights.
- Destructible objects where practical.

9. GRAPHICS AND AUDIO (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable original open-world crime-action game for Android, iOS, and desktop browsers, extending NEON HEIST.
- Validate and stabilize the game through build and browser testing.

## Requirements
- Original setting, characters, story, assets, music, vehicles, and missions; do not copy GTA content.
- Aim for an explorable 3D city with third-person gameplay, vehicles, police/wanted system, weapons, missions, NPCs, economy, smartphone, map, save/load, weather, and day/night.
- Support mobile touch and desktop controls; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Title: **NEON HEIST — Viceport Stories**, set in original Viceport City.
- Use Three.js, procedural world/assets, and synthesized audio in a browser game.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added procedural city, landmarks, vehicles, pedestrians, lighting, and day/night in `src/world.js`.
- Added 40 original mission titles and progression in `src/missions.js`.
- Extended `src/main.js` with gameplay bootstrap, movement, camera, driving, combat, wanted response, missions, map, HUD, phone apps, shop, save/settings, menus, and frame loop.
- Wired major UI interactions and mobile/desktop input paths.
- `npm run build` succeeds; Vite serves the app with HTTP 200.
- Verified `src/main.js` references 59 HTML IDs, all present in `index.html`; all referenced audio methods are defined.
- Headless Chromium rendered the landing page and screenshot without confirming gameplay interactions.

### Active
- Validate interactive gameplay and runtime behavior: menu start/continue, movement, phone, vehicles, missions, combat, save/load, and pause.
- Verify mobile controls and responsive layout; fix any issues discovered.

### Blocked
- Interactive browser testing remains unverified; available Chromium is headless, and no Playwright/Puppeteer or Chrome DevTools client package was found.

## Next Move
1. Run browser interaction tests at desktop and mobile viewport sizes, checking console/runtime errors and core gameplay flows.
2. Fix any issues discovered, then rerun `npm run build`.
3. Report verified gameplay scope and remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Main gameplay loop and UI wiring.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural city and world entities.
- `src/missions.js`: Mission data and progression.
- `index.html`: UI elements and IDs used by the game.
- `src/input.js`: Keyboard, mouse, and touch controls.
- `src/audio.js`: Synthesized audio APIs.
- `src/save.js`: Local save and settings helpers.
- `src/style.css`: UI styling and responsive layout.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; the working tree has untracked project files and `dist/` from the build.
- The production build emits a warning that the JavaScript chunk exceeds 500 kB (568.32 kB minified).
- Headless Chromium emitted DBus and software-WebGL/GPU warnings; the app rendered, but gameplay interactions have not been tested.
- Vite dev server was started with `npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1`.

## Objective
- Build and stabilize **NEON HEIST — Viceport Stories**, an original open-world crime-action browser game for Android, iOS, and desktop.
- Validate the playable experience and fix runtime or build issues.

## Requirements
- Original setting, characters, story, assets, music, vehicles, and missions; do not copy GTA content.
- Aim for an explorable 3D city with third-person gameplay, vehicles, wanted system, weapons, missions, NPCs, economy, smartphone, map, save/load, weather, and day/night.
- Support mobile touch and desktop controls; make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.

## Decisions
- Title: **NEON HEIST — Viceport Stories**, set in original Viceport City.
- Use Three.js, procedural world/assets, and synthesized audio in a browser game.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the procedural city, landmarks, vehicles, pedestrians, lighting/day-night, 40 original missions, gameplay systems, UI, and desktop/mobile input paths.
- Fixed startup runtime error by initializing `scene.background` to a `THREE.Color` in `src/world.js`.
- `npm run build` succeeds; Vite serves the app with HTTP 200.
- Headless Chromium/CDP verified map, phone/jobs app, mission acceptance, pause/resume, and mobile touch-control visibility; latest tested run reported zero runtime exceptions.
- Verified save/load round trip: `src/save.js` uses `neonheist.save.v1`; saving creates data, reload enables Continue, and Continue restores gameplay. The earlier failed check used the wrong key (`neon-heist-save`).

### Active
- Validate vehicle entry, driving, and exit using controlled positioning; ordinary walking from spawn did not encounter a vehicle.
- Exercise mobile touch stick, look, and action controls; visibility has been confirmed, but effects have not.

### Blocked
- Vehicle validation via a CDP debugger breakpoint script timed out; use a different controlled positioning/test method.

## Next Move
1. Position the player near a vehicle using a reliable CDP evaluation approach, then test entry, movement, and exit.
2. Send touch input to the mobile stick, look zone, and action buttons and confirm gameplay state changes.
3. Rerun `npm run build` after any fixes and report verified scope and remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Gameplay loop, mission/vehicle/combat/UI wiring, save/restore calls.
- `src/world.js`: Procedural world, vehicles, NPCs, mission markers, runtime update.
- `src/input.js`: Keyboard, pointer-lock mouse, and touch controls.
- `src/save.js`: Save keys and persistence implementation.
- `/tmp/opencode/neon_validate.py`: CDP gameplay and mobile visibility validation.
- `/tmp/opencode/neon_saveroundtrip.py`: CDP save/reload/continue test.
- `/tmp/opencode/neon_vehicle_debug.py`: Timed-out vehicle positioning experiment.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files and `dist/` are present in the working tree.
- Build emits a chunk-size warning: JavaScript bundle is about 568 kB minified.
- Existing vehicle interaction uses `KeyF`; player spawn is `(0, 13)`, and `nearestVehicle()` only finds vehicles within 6 units.
- Latest save round-trip restored `$2,400` and showed “Welcome back to Viceport.”
